subject: Hosted API regional SLO partitioning & transient-degradation carveout (APAC burst storms)
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha@blueharbor.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify APAC measurement epochs and carveout for burst storms

Hi Rishi —

Quick follow up from our SRE review this morning. Two asks before we can sign the term sheet:

1) Can Redwood regionalize latency measurement so APAC traffic is measured separately from US/EU? Our traffic patterns show hour-long burst storms tied to payroll processing windows that skew p95 when combined.
2) Is there a documented transient-degradation carveout for short-lived burst storms (we'd expect several 5–12 minute microstorms per month) so they don't trigger credit events?

If you have a short call tomorrow I can walk over our traffic graphs — would prefer to lock language rather than a broad "exceptions" clause.

Thanks,
Asha Rao
Head of Reliability, BlueHarbor Financial
ops@blueharbor.com

Attachment: bh-traffic-sample-june.csv (attachment stub)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify APAC measurement epochs and carveout for burst storms

Asha —

Thanks for the clear asks. We're happy to accommodate regional measurement and to define a tightly-scoped transient-degradation carveout. High level proposal:

- Regional measurement: p50/p95 measured per-region (US, EU, APAC) with independent epochs so cross-region bursts don't contaminate APAC SLOs.
- Transient-degradation carveout: allow a monthly aggregate of up to 30 minutes of "microstorm" carveout for APAC defined as contiguous intervals <= 15 minutes where system-level request queuing exceeds threshold X. Carveout would not apply to sustained degradations > 15 minutes.

I've looped in Marissa and Karthik to validate the operational implications and to draft precise wording for the SLA PDF. Can you share the sample graphs on the HubSpot link or the CSV you attached?

I'll follow up with a redline by EOD Monday.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, GTM Engineering 
Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai

Team —

Operational notes from infra:
- We can emit per-region quantile dashboards and measure p50/p95 per-region for hosted API (no backend change required).
- For the carveout, suggest changing the definition to: "up to 3 microstorm events per month, each <= 12 minutes, aggregated to 30 minutes total" to limit ambiguity.
- Need to define the detection trigger: propose "request latency moving average spikes > 3x baseline for the preceding 5-minute window".

I've attached a draft APAC SLO proposal with redlineable language. Karthik — please confirm we can automate sweep detection and reporting for carveout usage in console.

-Marissa
Head of Product, Redwood Console
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify APAC measurement epochs and carveout for burst storms

Confirming feasibility. Implementation notes:
- Measuring quantiles per-region: trivial with our existing routing tags. Will add a per-tenant per-region daily epoch export.
- Microstorm detection: we'll define a retriable rule and surface events in the Console under "SLO adjustments". We'll also record the microstorm as an event ID for audit and potential dispute resolution.
- Proposal for wording (for legal): "Transient-Degradation Carveout: For APAC traffic only, Redwood will exclude up to 3 transient degradation events per monthly billing period, each no longer than 12 minutes, with a combined aggregate exclusion not to exceed 30 minutes per month, provided that events are automatically detected by Redwood's monitoring and logged in the Console."

I'll push a redline to the PDF and request review.

-karthik
VP, Serving Runtime
karthik@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed SLA language for APAC regional SLOs and transient carveout

Asha —

Attached is the redlined SLA that implements the regional measurement and the transient-degradation carveout per our internal review. Highlights:

- Measurement: p50 and p95 are computed independently for traffic routed to APAC endpoints. Aggregation epoch = 1 minute; daily rollups used for monthly calculations.
- Carveout: "Transient-Degradation Carveout" (APAC only) — up to 3 events/month, each <= 12 minutes, 30 minutes aggregate/month. Events are detected by Redwood monitoring (3x baseline rule) and logged with event IDs and start/end timestamps. Excluded intervals will be omitted from monthly p95 computation.
- Reporting: Console will show carveout usage and include downloadable event logs for audit.

If that language works for BlueHarbor we will attach it to the term sheet and begin the DocuSign flow. If you want tweaks, call today at 3pm PT and we can finalize.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, GTM Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: 20270714-Redwood-SLA-redline-for-blueharbor.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Asha Rao <asha@blueharbor.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@blueharbor.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA language for APAC regional SLOs and transient carveout

Rishi —

This looks great and exactly the level of specificity we need. Two small asks:

- Can you make the detection threshold configurable for enterprise customers (we may want 2.5x for peak-payroll windows)?
- Please add a clause that carveout events are not eligible for credit if traffic shaping from our side contributes >20% of the latency (we'll provide netflow samples on request).

If you can add those tweaks in a single redline, I'll route for legal review and we can sign this week. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Asha
Head of Reliability, BlueHarbor Financial
